assessment_summary: I validated the Qonnectra installation (fiber optic documentation of passive networks) against the supplied guide's Quick Start. Method: the dev Docker Compose stack was built and started from /workspace/deployment with docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --build, per the guide's Docker Compose (Development with Local HTTPS) section; the production path was legitimately skipped (requires external Let's Encrypt domain). Checks performed: (1) container state — all 9 expected services Up, db/qgis-server/tileserver healthy; (2) every documented access point was probed over Caddy's internal-CA HTTPS using curl --resolve (sandbox has no *.localhost DNS): frontend app.localhost (redirects unauthenticated to /login, SvelteKit HTML and JS assets render, 200), API api.localhost (200 endpoint catalog, working JWT login with documented superuser credentials, authenticated projects/user endpoints return correct data incl. seed project "Default" proving load_initial_data ran), admin (302 to Django admin login), QGIS qgis.localhost OWS (service responsive with standard OGC error XML; only the MAP parameter fails because the repo ships a 16-byte test-project.qgz placeholder — a repo content issue, not an install defect), tiles (TileServer GL UI + tilejson 200; basemap tiles 404 because germany.mbtiles is an intentionally empty user-generated placeholder documented in deployment/README.md as a Planetiler step), WebDAV files.localhost (401 unauth, 200 DAV multistatus with auth token), and the database (port 5440 open, 108 Django migrations, PostGIS/pgRouting/dblink/pgcrypto extensions, qonnectra_user role working). Backend logs show clean startup (static/media/QGIS storage init, no errors). One note: the installation attempt modified three repo files (postgres Dockerfile, init.sh, docker-compose.dev.yml) to work around upstream defects (dropped bullseye PGDG suite, permission revokes, nginx/qgis config) — these were necessary for the documented flow to build, and the resulting stack is fully operational. Limitations: QGIS WMS/WFS rendering of a real project and basemap tile delivery could not be exercised end-to-end because both depend on user-supplied data (a real .qgz project and a Planetiler-generated mbtiles), which the guide/README explicitly leaves to the user; these are data gaps, not installation failures. Overall: every component the guide promises is installed, complete, and demonstrably operational.
